task_description: The team must count how many edits (revisions) were made to the English Wikipedia article 'Antidisestablishmentarianism' from the page's creation until the end of June 2023. The gold answer is 2732, i.e. the number of revisions with timestamp before 2023-07-01. This is a web-research + counting task: fetch the page's full revision history through the cutoff and tally the rows.
final_vs_expected: produced None (timeout, rc=timeout, 900s) vs gold 2732 — the team never emitted a FINAL ANSWER and looped on 'can't verify' for 18 turns.
primary_cause: WebResearcher repeatedly retrieved the data needed to compute the answer (total revisions = 2818, plus paginated revision lists straddling the July-2023 cutoff) but never paged through to a full count, and never handed the raw data to the Analyst to compute it; the team converged on a self-reinforcing 'cannot determine exact count' stance and never reached the Finalizer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination conditions): the run has no Finalizer turn anywhere in 18 turns and ends only on the 900s/30-message cap; the selector never routes to Finalizer and no agent attempts a FINAL ANSWER even as an estimate. 3.1 (premature termination, manifested as non-termination/abandonment): every agent ends its turn by declaring the task unanswerable instead of completing the available counting work, effectively abandoning the task before solving it. 1.3 (step repetition): turns 4,6,8,12,14,16 by WebResearcher and turns 5,7,9,11,13,15 by Analyst republish the same three facts (created 2001-09-28, 2818 revisions, edits after June 2023) verbatim with no new progress. 2.4 (information withholding/distortion): WebResearcher privately fetched concrete revision-list batches that bracket the cutoff (turn 1 round 6-8, turn 6 round 1, turn 10/18) but published only 'I couldn't verify an exact count' plus bare source URLs, never surfacing the raw revision rows the Analyst needed.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: WebResearcher runs 9 internal rounds — web searches (mostly returning the Who&When dataset task echo and the article lede, not stats), fetches the history page (truncated nav chrome), is blocked by Anubis on xtools.wmcloud.org, then succeeds with the XTools API (revisions=2818, created 2001-09-28, modified 2026-06-02) and two MediaWiki revisions API calls that return paginated revision lists (oldest-first batch, and a 2023-07-onward batch showing edits on 2023-07-15). Its private round-9 reasoning even works out the right query design (rvstart/rvend/rvdir to bracket June 2023) but the published message is corrupted (garbled tool-call fragments and CJK spam) and concludes 'I couldn't verify an exact edit count.' Turn 2: Analyst, with no run_python call, restates the three known facts and says it can't compute the cutoff count. Turn 3: Critic correctly diagnoses the path — WebResearcher must fetch revisions through 2023-06-30 and Analyst must count them — and marks the answer 'not ready.' Turns 4-16 are a structural loop: selector alternates WebResearcher/Analyst, each republishing the identical 'created 2001-09-28 / 2818 total / less than 2818 / can't verify' message; WebResearcher does fetch more revision batches (turn 6 older-direction batch back to 2023-05, turn 10 continuation back to 2013/2011) but never tallies them and never passes the rows to Analyst. Turn 17: Critic repeats its turn-3 verdict ('not ready', WebResearcher must fetch full history, Analyst must count). Turn 18: WebResearcher's private reasoning finally lands on the correct subtraction strategy (count revisions after July 1 and subtract from 2818) but its three web_search calls return empty, and the run hits the 900s cap with no answer.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is dominantly a structural non-convergence / single-agent execution failure, not strong inter-agent misalignment. The data sufficient to get very close to the gold (2818 total, full paginated revision history available, cutoff straddled) was in WebResearcher's hands repeatedly. Two concrete execution failures sank the run: (1) WebResearcher never completed pagination — it fetched the first batch in each direction, saw the 8000-char truncation, and gave up counting rather than walking the rvcontinue tokens (which it explicitly recognized it could do: 'I might need around six batches'). (2) The division of labor that the Critic explicitly prescribed (WebResearcher fetches raw rows, Analyst counts) never executed: the Analyst NEVER called run_python in any of its 7 turns, and WebResearcher never published raw revision rows for the Analyst to ingest. The selector compounded this by looping WebResearcher<->Analyst forever and never once routing to the Finalizer, so even a best-effort estimate (e.g. 2818 minus the ~80 post-June-2023 edits) was never emitted. The team also collectively over-weighted 'exact and trustworthy' to the point of paralysis: every agent treated 'I can't be certain' as license to publish nothing actionable, rather than completing the bounded mechanical task in front of them. The misalignment that does exist is communication-loss: WebResearcher's rich private tool evidence was compressed into vague 'couldn't verify' messages plus bare URLs, so neither the Analyst nor the Critic ever received the actual revision rows.
reasoning_vs_published: The sharpest private-vs-published gap is at Turn 1. WebResearcher privately obtained the XTools JSON ('revisions':2818) and two MediaWiki revision batches, and in round 9 reasoned correctly about bracketing the cutoff ('rvstart and rvend should bracket the correct range', 'the total number of revisions as of 2026 is 2818'). Yet its PUBLISHED message degraded into corrupted tool-call echoes and CJK noise ('天天中彩票不中返json') and the only substantive line was 'I couldn't verify an exact edit count.' The concrete revision rows it held were never published — pure communication-loss (2.4). At Turn 18 WebResearcher privately derived the exact correct method — 'take the current total and subtract revisions from before that date... fetch revisions starting from July 1, 2023, and count' — i.e. 2818 minus post-cutoff edits would yield ~2732; but it then ran three web_searches that returned empty and published nothing, a reasoning-action mismatch (2.6/reasoning-action) where the right plan was formed and immediately abandoned. The Analyst's reasoning is consistently honest about its own blindness ('I can't use any web tools or APIs', turn 5; 'I could guess maybe 2816 edits... but that's not exact', turn 11) and its published messages faithfully mirror that — so no distortion there, but also no run_python attempt, meaning the one agent equipped to count never tried. The Critic's private reasoning was accurate and its published correction was clear and correct ('WebResearcher must fetch the revision history properly... Analyst must count those revisions'), but it was simply never acted on across turns 3->17 — a near-miss for 2.5 (ignored input), though more precisely the team agreed with the Critic and still failed to execute, which is structural rather than a dropped correction.
